brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at the very same corner of the same cell as a spike, touching
requirements.evidence: Configurator forbids it - addNotch at the spike's junction is refused with SPIKE_CLASH; build keeps spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 and drawer notch:0#1,1#notch2 at different junction (1,1 k=2) to stay mesh-clear.

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell as the drawer, touching
requirements.evidence: Same SPIKE_CLASH rule: spike needs three touching cells around junction, drawer occupies the empty slot at that junction. Closest achievable is offset - built spike at level 0 junction 0,0/0,1/1,0, drawer nearby but not co-located.

finish.summary: Built 3 bases to create valid spike and notch sockets, placed spike at J0,0|0,1|1,0 and notch drawer frame at 1,1. Same-corner touching is not configurable - configurator enforces SPIKE_CLASH and returns no valid socket for co-location. Mesh is clear but requirement is unmet by rule.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
